content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, nakedness primarily symbolizes shame, guilt, and the exposure of sin before God — the human condition after the Fall, in which people are spiritually destitute and need to be 'covered' or clothed by God (ultimately with Christ's righteousness). The movement from unashamed nakedness in Eden, to shame-filled awareness of nakedness after sin, to God clothing Adam and Eve, is treated as the paradigm: nakedness = exposed sinfulness and shame; divine clothing = grace, atonement, and imputed righteousness.","primary_basis":["Genesis 2:25 (naked and not ashamed before the Fall)","Genesis 3:7 (eyes opened, they knew they were naked)","Genesis 3:10-11 ('I was afraid, because I was naked')","Genesis 3:21 (God clothes them with garments of skin)","Revelation 3:17-18 (Laodicea: 'wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked... buy white garments so that the shame of your nakedness may not be seen')","Revelation 16:15 (blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and be exposed)","Hebrews 4:13 (all things naked and exposed before God's eyes)","Isaiah 61:10 / 2 Corinthians 5:21 (being clothed with garments of salvation / righteousness as the remedy)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Innocence and unfallen purity: before the Fall, nakedness without shame symbolizes original innocence, integrity, and unbroken intimacy with God and one another (emphasized in patristic writers and in John Paul II's 'theology of the body').","basis":["Genesis 2:25","Genesis 3:7 (by contrast)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Divine judgment and public humiliation: in the prophets, stripping a nation or unfaithful 'wife' naked symbolizes God's judgment, disgrace, and exile.","basis":["Isaiah 47:2-3","Ezekiel 16:35-39; 23:26-29","Hosea 2:3","Nahum 3:5","Lamentations 1:8","Micah 1:8-11"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Vulnerability, poverty, and human helplessness: nakedness stands for material destitution and the creaturely condition in which humans enter and leave the world, grounding the call to clothe the naked as an act of mercy.","basis":["Job 1:21","Ecclesiastes 5:15","Matthew 25:36-44","James 2:15-16","Isaiah 58:7","Job 22:6; 24:7-10"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Euphemism for sexual relations or sexual sin: 'uncovering nakedness' in the Levitical codes denotes illicit sexual intercourse, and some interpreters extend this to symbolic readings of dishonor (e.g., Ham and Noah).","basis":["Leviticus 18:6-19; 20:11-21","Genesis 9:20-25","Ezekiel 16 and 23 (adultery imagery)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The disembodied or mortal state awaiting resurrection: Paul uses being 'found naked' for existence without the resurrection body, longing to be 'further clothed.'","basis":["2 Corinthians 5:2-4","1 Corinthians 15:37 (bare/naked seed imagery)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Prophetic sign-act or ecstatic abandonment: going naked as an enacted prophetic sign of coming captivity or, in Saul's case, unusual prophetic behavior.","basis":["Isaiah 20:2-4","Micah 1:8","1 Samuel 19:24"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"The consensus is strong but two-sided: nakedness before the Fall symbolizes innocence, while after the Fall it symbolizes shame, guilt, and exposure needing divine covering. Most Christian teaching integrates both under a single arc (innocence lost, shame exposed, righteousness restored through God's clothing), with the shame/exposure/need-for-covering sense dominating sermonic and theological usage, reinforced by Revelation 3:17-18. The alternative senses (judgment, poverty, sexual euphemism, disembodiment) are well-recognized contextual meanings rather than rivals to the primary symbol; interpreters generally treat them as distinct uses in their respective genres. Note that 'uncovering nakedness' in Leviticus is usually classed as a legal idiom rather than a symbol per se."}
